key_insight: Preserving dual potentials during Sinkhorn annealing enables subsequential convergence to an optimal transport solution under a sharp non-summability condition, with full convergence under an additional schedule condition.
engineering_relevance: Linear inverse-temperature schedules satisfy the potential-preserving convergence conditions even where scaling-preserving annealing can fail.
method: Decrease entropic regularisation while preserving dual potentials rather than multiplicative scaling factors.
Require positive, non-increasing regularisation tending to zero with a divergent sum for subsequential convergence.
Establish full convergence when relative inverse-temperature increments are also square-summable, plus rates for polynomial inverse-temperature growth up to linear.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence proofs, counterexamples, improved rounded transport-cost gap rates over scaling-preserving annealing, and simple numerical illustrations.
watch_item: Non-summability alone does not ensure full convergence; summable schedules can converge to plans violating the prescribed source marginal.
paper_title: Convergence of potential-preserving annealed Sinkhorn algorithm
